topStories.headline: Mystery 'Marina Park' Flyers Blanket the Neighborhood — Nobody Knows Who Made Them
topStories.dek: AI-generated leaflets promoting a car-free Marina Boulevard and 900-plus new homes have appeared across the Marina District, but the group named on them has no record with city ethics regulators.
topStories.body:
Thousands of leaflets appeared on windshields and doorsteps across the Marina District over the past week, promoting a proposal to permanently close all four lanes of Marina Boulevard to private vehicles and build more than 900 homes on the freed-up land. The flyers show families walking through a car-free waterfront park with an unobstructed view of the Golden Gate Bridge and describe the concept as directly inspired by the Sunset Dunes conversion of the Great Highway.

At the bottom of each leaflet, a disclosure box states the ad is paid for by 'Friends of Marina Park' and lists the SF Bicycle Coalition, Sunset Dunes Park, and the No on G campaign as aligned supporters. But the San Francisco Ethics Commission has no record of any committee or filer by that name, and none of the organizations listed as partners have heard of the group. The SF Bicycle Coalition confirmed it did not endorse the proposal and did not approve the use of its logo on the flyer.

Align Real Estate, the developer behind the proposed 848-unit Marina Safeway redevelopment, declined to comment beyond saying it was the first time the firm had seen the flyer. The SF Standard, which broke the story on October 15, reported the leaflets appear to be AI-generated. Who commissioned or distributed them remains unknown.

The episode adds a disorienting new layer to an already fractious debate over the future of the Marina waterfront, where the fate of the Safeway site, the Gashouse Cove remediation project, and now an anonymous urbanist campaign are all competing for residents' attention simultaneously.

topStories.headline: Safeway Federal Lawsuit Presses On as City's 90-Day Approval Clock Winds Down
topStories.dek: With the Planning Department on a ministerial deadline expiring around mid-November, the federal suit challenging the 848-unit Marina Safeway project on contamination and streamlining grounds remains before the court.
topStories.body:
The federal lawsuit filed September 11 against the proposed Marina Safeway redevelopment remains active in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The suit was brought by the YesAND Foundation, Neighborhoods United San Francisco, and four Marina District residents, and names developer Align Real Estate Partners, the city of San Francisco, its Public Health and Planning Departments, PG&E, and Safeway parent company Albertsons as defendants. The complaint alleges that city officials improperly approved the project under Assembly Bill 2011 while allowing Align to bypass a full investigation of toxic contamination at 15 Marina Blvd., and asks the court to halt the project until those reviews are complete.

That legal fight runs alongside a planning process on its own hard deadline. In mid-August, the San Francisco Planning Department determined the project met AB 2011's eligibility requirements, closing the first of two 90-day review stages. The department now has until around mid-November to formally approve or deny the project on a ministerial basis — a high-level land-use decision that, if granted, would allow Align to then pursue building permits covering earthquake, liquefaction, and contamination details. The city has said it will review the suit when officially served; Align has maintained the project meets all state requirements.

Opponents, led by the Marina Community Association and the Cow Hollow Association, argue the city cannot assess whether contamination can be safely managed while more than 40,000 square feet beneath the existing Safeway store remains untested — a gap Align's own environmental consultant has acknowledged, attributing it to the need to wait until the operating store closes. The Planning Director has said AB 2011's environmental requirements will be satisfied later in the permitting and construction process, not as a precondition for approval. Whether the federal court intervenes before the planning clock expires is now the central question for neighbors watching the case.

topStories.headline: Fall Dredge Is Under Way at the Marina Yacht Harbor; Channel Open With Caution
topStories.dek: SF Rec & Park's October 15 weekly harbor update confirms the long-anticipated fall dredging began at the West Entry Channel on or after October 13, with work expected to run through November.
topStories.body:
The fall dredging episode at the San Francisco Marina Yacht Harbor's West Entry Channel is now under way, according to the SF Recreation and Parks Department's weekly harbor update published October 15. The department had anticipated the work would begin on or shortly after October 13 and expects completion in November — the second dredging episode of 2026 after the spring episode wrapped up June 28.

As of Thursday morning the channel was open, but mariners are asked to navigate with caution. The most recent sounding showed a channel width of approximately 75 feet at a tide height of 3.4 feet, measured at 8:30 a.m. Harbor staff flagged that sand conditions near the north entrance continue to shift with tidal movement and urged extra caution at low water. Combined with the spring episode, dredging has removed 38,710 cubic yards of sediment from the waterway entrance sea floor to date, increasing depth and improving navigation safety. Rec & Park will continue publishing weekly sounding reports every Thursday and will provide pre-dredge and post-dredge bathymetric surveys to berth holders for reference.

The current maintenance dredging is separate from the larger $190 million Marina Improvement and Remediation Project (MIRP), which the Rec & Park Commission approved in concept design in April. That broader effort — transforming Gashouse Cove into a five-acre waterfront park, building new breakwaters in both harbors, and remediating PG&E contamination from a 19th-century manufactured gas plant — is still in detailed design. Rec & Park expects to advertise the construction contract this fall, with construction slated to begin in mid-2027.

moreNews.headline: Sherrill Faces Three Challengers in November 3 District 2 Race
moreNews.body: Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, who represents Marina, Pacific Heights, Cow Hollow, and Presidio Heights, is seeking a full four-year term in the November 3 ranked-choice election. Sherrill was appointed to the seat in December 2024 after former Supervisor Catherine Stefani won election to the California State Assembly, and won a June 2026 special election with approximately 69 percent of the vote. He now faces property management executive Nicholas Berg, community advocate Monthanus Ratanapakdee, and restaurant manager Guy McCoy on the November ballot. His main June opponent, Lori Brooke, opted not to run again. Candidate information is available at the SF Chronicle's 2026 Bay Area Voter Guide.

moreNews.headline: Marina Branch Library Open House Planned This Month — Date to Be Confirmed
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Public Library's October 2026 newsletter confirms Marina Branch at 1890 Chestnut Street is hosting an open house this month as part of a citywide library celebration. Planned activities include an SF Bicycle Coalition smoothie bike, a BINGO tournament, a fire truck visit, a kids-and-pets costume swap, and a Giant Bubbles party in the courtyard. The newsletter did not publish a specific date; residents should check sfpl.org/locations/marina or call 415-355-2823 to confirm the date and time.
moreNews.sourceName: San Francisco Public Library — At the Library, October 2026
